I searched the working directory (`C:/Users/pujan/AppData/Local/Temp`) but couldn't find a prompt file whose output instruction says to "write a telegram" — the only telegram hits were unrelated repo/docs files. Can you point me to the exact prompt file?

That said, if a prompt's output spec literally tells the model to "write a telegram," here's what I'd change in general:

- **Rename/redefine the format** — "telegram" is ambiguous (Telegram app message? old-school telegraph style?). Replace it with an explicit output spec: audience, tone, length limit, and structure (e.g., "a plain-text message under 280 characters, no markdown").
- **Specify constraints concretely** — max length, whether salutations/sign-offs are allowed, allowed formatting (Markdown vs plain text), language, and what to omit (preamble, explanations after the message).
- **Add a format example** — one short example of the desired output beats a paragraph of description.
- **Make the contract machine-checkable** if the output is parsed downstream (e.g., "reply with only the message body; no quotes, no code fences"), so the pipeline can validate or reject non-conforming output.

Share the file path and I'll give specific line-level suggestions instead of these general ones.

I'd keep status questions read-only: answer with the current state (what's done, what's pending, blockers) and stop there. Treating "how's it going?" as a standing goal turns a report into implicit permission to keep making changes — scope creep with no new instruction behind it. So: answer the status, propose next steps as options, and only act once a change is actually requested. Per your instruction, I'm not touching any files.

I don't actually see the pasted text in your message, so I'd answer generally. In a terminal-only context I'd: - Drop the webview/HTML directives (inline CSS, ``/`` tags, styled panels, emoji-decorated callouts) — nothing renders them. - Keep the substance: plain ASCII text, short paragraphs, `-` bullets, indented code blocks with no syntax highlighting assumed. - Replace link/rich-media references with bare URLs or file paths. - Keep line width ~80 cols so nothing wraps oddly. - Retain the behavioral rules (tone, scope, "no file edits") since those apply anywhere. Paste the actual text and I'll give the specific line-by-line edits.
